{
  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk that increasingly powerful AI outpaces people's ability to adjust and researchers' ability to understand it, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "Release AI systems in stages, withholding each successor until society has fully adapted to the current system and alignment researchers have learned everything they can from it. Repeating this release-and-wait cycle gives society time to adjust to less powerful AI and researchers time to study existing systems before confronting more capable ones. The proposed benefit comes from these substantive pauses, not merely from releasing successive systems in quick succession.",
  "spans": [
    "If you really wanted this kind of gradual release that lets society adjust to less powerful AI, you would do something like this:",
    "Release AI #1",
    "Wait until society has fully adapted to it, and alignment researchers have learned everything they can from it.",
    "Then release AI #2",
    "Nobody thinks society has even partially adapted to any of these, or that alignment researchers have done more than begin to study them."
  ]
}
